name: Mohamed Al-Begaowe
headline: PhD Researcher in Statistical Physics & Computational Neuroscience | Boston College
summary: Physics PhD researcher at Boston College working at the intersection of statistical physics, machine learning theory, and computational neuroscience. I study how neural networks learn and generalize across tasks using replica methods, manifold geometry, and large-scale HPC experiments. I work across the full research stack — from mathematical theory to building reproducible Python pipelines and managing compute workflows on HPC clusters. I collaborate across physics, neuroscience, and ML.

experience.description: Support research computing operations on the Andromeda HPC cluster. Automate usage reporting, assist researchers with cluster workflows, and maintain computational infrastructure supporting various research groups.

experience.org: Boston College — Dept. of Psychology & Neuroscience
experience.description: Theoretical and computational study of multi-task neural representations using statistical physics and ML. Supervisor: Dr. Stefano Anzellotti. Investigating multi-task learning in visual recognition through a manifold-theoretic framework, focusing on invariance, separability, and storage capacity of object manifolds in trained neural networks. Implementing experiments in PyTorch; analyzing the geometry of learned representations across systematically varied task configurations.

Supervisors: Dr. Benedetta Flebus · Dr. Krzysztof Kempa. Co-authored peer-reviewed publication on Non-Hermitian and Liouvillian skin effects in magnetic systems (Physical Review B, 2025). Designed and simulated therapeutic ultrasound–piezoelectric nanoparticle experiments using COMSOL Multiphysics.
Project: Investigation and modeling of neutron/X-ray reflection by thin films of polymer nanocomposites. Computational modeling of wave reflection behavior in multilayer nanocomposite thin films.

Covered topics including machine learning for physics, generative models, and AI-driven scientific discovery. Hackathon project MMCRepLearn: compared self-supervised methods (MMCR vs. SimCLR) for classification on particle physics datasets using PyTorch.
